claims.claim: urllib3 can automatically retry idempotent requests.
claims.citation: urllib3 can automatically retry idempotent requests.

claims.claim: The urllib3 retry mechanism also handles redirects.
claims.citation: This same mechanism also handles redirects.

claims.claim: The retries parameter of urllib3's request() controls retries.
claims.citation: You can control the retries using the retries parameter to request().

claims.claim: By default, urllib3 retries requests 3 times.
claims.citation: By default, urllib3 will retry requests 3 times

claims.claim: By default, urllib3 follows up to 3 redirects.
Specifying an integer as the retries parameter of urllib3's request() changes the number of retries.
claims.citation: To change the number of retries just specify an integer

claims.claim: Specifying retries=False in urllib3's request() disables all retry and redirect logic.
claims.citation: To disable all retry and redirect logic specify retries=False

claims.claim: Specifying redirect=False in urllib3's request() disables redirects.
claims.citation: To disable redirects but keep the retrying logic, specify redirect=False

claims.claim: Specifying redirect=False in urllib3's request() keeps the retrying logic.
claims.citation: To disable redirects but keep the retrying logic, specify redirect=False

claims.claim: A urllib3 Retry instance can be passed as the retries parameter for more granular control over retries.
claims.citation: For more granular control you can use a Retry instance.

claims.claim: The urllib3 Retry class allows far greater control of how requests are retried.
claims.citation: This class allows you far greater control of how requests are retried.

claims.claim: A urllib3 Retry instance can be used to do a total of 3 retries while limiting redirects to only 2.
claims.citation: to do a total of 3 retries, but limit to only 2 redirects

claims.claim: urllib3 can be configured to not raise exceptions for too many redirects and instead return the 302 response.
claims.citation: You can also disable exceptions for too many redirects and just return the 302 response

claims.claim: A retry policy can be specified at the urllib3 PoolManager level so that all requests are subject to the same retry policy.
claims.citation: If you want all requests to be subject to the same retry policy, you can specify the retry at the PoolManager level

claims.claim: A pool-level retry policy set on a urllib3 PoolManager can be overridden by specifying retries to request().
claims.citation: You can still override this pool-level retry policy by specifying retries to request().
